question: Patients on maintenance haemodialysis typically report impairment in physical, psychological, and social quality-of-life domains, with fatigue and time burden being among the most frequently cited concerns.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Haemodialysis affects quality of life across all domains — physical (fatigue, uraemia, anaemia), psychological (depression, anxiety), and social (time burden, travel restrictions, employment). Fatigue and time-on-dialysis commitment are among the most prominent patient-reported concerns.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. CKD and haemodialysis impose a profound multi-domain QoL burden. Physical domain: fatigue, uraemic symptoms, anaemia, dialysis-related hypotension. Psychological domain: depression, anxiety, loss of identity/control. Social domain: dietary restrictions, inability to travel, reduced employment, strain on relationships. Time burden (3× weekly HD, 4h sessions) is consistently rated as the most disruptive factor by patients.
